hyps.why: Adding a conv where there was no edge adds both capacity and a new path to the output, so it gains more than replacing an existing op.
Removing the direct input-to-output edge is much more damaging when the node-2-to-output edge is also missing, because the output then depends on node 1 alone or becomes disconnected.
When node 1 has no direct edge to the output, a conv on the input-to-node-1 edge reaches the output only indirectly, so it helps less.
If node 2 does not feed the output, operations entering node 2 have no effect on the output.
The node-1-to-node-2 conv is dead computation when node 2 is disconnected from the output.
If node 1 receives no input, any operation on the edge from node 1 to the output processes zeros.
Turning a missing edge into a conv adds a new path and capacity, which gains more than replacing skip or pooling.
Adding a residual connection where there was none improves gradient flow far more than replacing an existing conv or pooling op on that edge.
Removing the node-2-to-output edge when the node-1-to-output edge is already missing leaves only the direct input edge, so the cell collapses to a shallow network.
Filling an empty input-to-node-2 edge with a conv adds a new path and parameters, giving a larger gain than replacing an existing op.
